body:
Let's formulate the task.

I want some software, that is available as library, CLI, micro service, and GitHub Pages static web app.

It should use Rust + WebAssembly + React.js on web. https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments in CLI, https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation for all internal end external data representation, https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic for conversion of natural language to formal expressions, to check if they are computable, and also to compute them. For https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs data operations (like database, semantic network / web), that can lazily load data from wikidata, like https://github.com/link-assistant/human-language does.

It should be able to take as input any human language, and try to convert it formal form. At least we should be able to see, what formal version of statement depends on (other statements), what statements depend on it (other statements). Based on its and dependent statements probability - given some system (belief system or formal system, by default something commonly agreeable scientific) - user should be able to configure such system. So for each statement using best of public knowledge (wikipedia, wikidata) we should be able to find disprovements of the statement and confirmations, meaning we should calculate total probability that this statement is true, and also list confirmations and refutations.

And if end only if the statement is specific enough to be converted to formal expression we can show result.

For example:

`1 + 1 = 1` should be 0%, and `1 + 1 = 2` should be 100% in default belief/formal system.

Everything else that relies to real world data should be calculated in probability.

We should also support as in https://github.com/link-assistant/model-in-browser for different formulations of the same statement or language expression.

So we can simplify the UI for the user, so it can use both LLMs and algorithms to generate alternatives/more specific variants to remove ambiguity.

So the end result would be a tool, that will be as logical counterpart for intuitive neural networks, to improve quality of fact checking, reasoning and so on. That should also be possible to use that tool as general calculator https://github.com/link-assistant/calculator, or even programming language, or tool for translation between languages as we do in github.com/link-assistant/human-language.

There much more potential to it, but I want to have a functional playground, so I can iterate on it.

Please in the same style of my message, trying to be as short as possible add any missing content from all we discussed previously, so I can add it to the issue, on GitHub and as AI to implement MVP.

Here is a concise, same-style extension you can append to your issue (only missing pieces, tightened, implementation-oriented):

⸻

We should explicitly support multi-interpretation pipeline:

* For each input statement:
    * generate top N (3–10) interpretations (LLM + rules)
    * cluster similar meanings
    * present user selectable options (not raw formal logic, but paraphrases + examples)
    * only after selection → convert to formal expression

⸻

We must support underspecified / partial formalization:

* if statement is not fully formalizable:
    * represent as constraints / partial graph
    * mark unknown / ambiguous parts
    * allow progressive refinement

⸻

We need dependency graph (core primitive):

* nodes = statements (formal or semi-formal)
* edges:
    * depends_on
    * implies
    * contradicts
    * supports / refutes
* must support:
    * forward dependencies
    * reverse dependencies
    * minimal dependency extraction

⸻

We need belief / probability layer:

* probability is NOT truth, but confidence
* configurable belief systems:
    * default: scientific consensus (Wikipedia / Wikidata)
    * custom user-defined systems
* each statement:
    * P(true)
    * list of supporting statements
    * list of contradicting statements
* probability propagation:
    * through dependency graph
    * weighted by source reliability

⸻

We must define evidence model:

* sources:
    * Wikidata (structured)
    * Wikipedia (text → extracted claims)
* each claim:
    * provenance (source, reference)
    * confidence weight
* lazy loading via doublets-rs

⸻

We need ambiguity-aware reasoning:

* each statement may have multiple interpretations
* reasoning operates on:
    * selected interpretation OR
    * top-k interpretations (optional)
* avoid combinatorial explosion:
    * prune by probability / relevance

⸻

We need normalization / equivalence layer:

* detect:
    * equivalent statements
    * paraphrases
    * logical equivalence
* merge into same node when possible

⸻

We need formalization levels:

1. raw text
2. structured meaning (graph / links-notation)
3. partial formal expression
4. fully computable expression

Only level (4) → executable

⸻

We need execution layer:

* if computable:
    * evaluate (calculator / program)
* if not:
    * estimate probability via evidence

⸻

We need UI constraints:

* never show raw logic first
* always show:
    * natural language interpretations
    * examples of differences
* allow:
    * user selection
    * refinement (“make more specific”)

⸻

We need LLM role clearly bounded:

* generate interpretations
* suggest refinements
* extract candidate formal structures
* NOT source of truth

⸻

We need core invariants:

* everything is a graph
* everything is versioned
* everything has provenance
* no hidden assumptions

⸻

We need MVP scope (strict):

* input → generate 3 interpretations
* user selects one
* convert to simple formal form (math / basic logic)
* build dependency graph (manual + small auto)
* fetch limited Wikidata evidence
* compute naive probability:
    * (#support − #refute) / total weighted
* visualize:
    * statement
    * dependencies
    * probability

⸻

We explicitly do NOT solve (yet):

* full natural language understanding
* complete ambiguity coverage
* perfect probability model
* large-scale graph optimization

⸻

Goal:

interactive “logic + probability + meaning selection” playground
bridging natural language ↔ formal reasoning

We need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).
title: First prototype
